g.data-info: Waxy waterproof layer covering the epidermis, thicker on the upper surface.
Single layer of transparent cells, usually without stomata, that protects the leaf.
Tightly packed column-shaped cells full of chloroplasts where most photosynthesis happens.
Irregular, loosely arranged cells with fewer chloroplasts and many air spaces between them.
Gaps between spongy cells, including the large substomatal chamber, through which gases diffuse.
A ring of parenchyma cells tightly surrounding the vein.
Upper side of the vein; its vessels bring water into the leaf.
Lower side of the vein; it carries sugars made in the leaf to the rest of the plant.
Bottom layer of cells, which contains most of the stomata.
A pore bordered by two bean-shaped guard cells that open and close it to control gas exchange and water loss.
